examples: The computer analyst was glad to have chosen a field in which jobs were abundant.
The recruiter was surprised by the abundant number of qualified applicants.
The success of the company was based on its early accomplishments.
In honor of her accomplishments, the manager was promoted.
Every year, the firm brings together its top lawyers and its newest recruits for a training session.
Our goal this year is to bring together the most creative group we can find.

vocabulary.definition: one being considered for a position, office, or award
examples: The recruiter will interview all candidates for the position.
The president of our company is a candidate for the Outstanding Business Award.

vocabulary.definition: to plan, to invent, to think of
examples: In order for that small business to succeed, it needs to come up with a new strategy.
How was the new employee able to come up with that cost-cutting idea after only one week on the job?

vocabulary.definition: in proportion to, corresponding, equal to
examples: Generally the first year's salary is commensurate with experience and education level.
As mentioned in your packets, the number of new recruits will be commensurate with the number of vacancies at the company.

vocabulary.definition: a fit, a similarity; to put together, to fit
examples: It is difficult to make a decision when both candidates seem to be a perfect match.
A headhunter matches qualified candidates to suitable positions.

vocabulary.definition: a group of characteristics or traits
examples: The recruiter told him that, unfortunately, he did not fit the job profile.
As jobs change, so does the company's profile for the job candidate.

vocabulary.definition: requirements, qualities, or abilities needed for something
examples: The job seeker had done extensive volunteer work and was able to add this experience to his list of qualifications.
The applicant had so many qualifications that the company created a new position for her.

vocabulary.definition: to attract people to join an organization or a cause; a person who is recruited
examples: When the consulting firm recruited her, they offered to pay her relocation expenses.
The new recruits spent the entire day in training.
Submit your résumé to the human resources department.
The applicant submitted all her paperwork in a professional and timely manner.

vocabulary.definition: taking up a lot of time, lengthy
examples: Even though it was time-consuming, all of the participants felt that the open house was very worthwhile.
Five interviews later, Ms. Lopez had the job, but it was the most time-consuming process she had ever gone through.
